Modeller inference, not stated by ATO: $62,500 = $30,000 concessional cap x 100 / 12% / 4 quarters, i.e. the cap-linked formula appears to apply to the 2025-26 figure; the ATO ties the formula to 'from 1 July 2026'. BASIS CHANGE: from 1 July 2026 (Payday Super) the maximum contribution base is an ANNUAL amount of qualifying earnings per financial year, not a per-quarter figure. ATO: 2026-27 = $270,830 (also stated at https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/super-for-employers/paying-super-on-payday/what-payments-are-qualifying-earnings/maximum-contributions-base). Formula (ATO): concessional contributions cap x 100 / charge percentage, rounded down to nearest $10 = 32,500 x 100 / 12 = 270,833.33 -> 270,830. Do not divide by 4 to compare with earlier per-quarter rows; ATO publishes no quarterly equivalent. Once qualifying earnings reach the base the employer can stop minimum SG for that year. Next year's value moves with the concessional cap and the SG rate.

transfer_balance_cap.unit: AUD (general transfer balance cap, per financial year)
transfer_balance_cap.meaning: General transfer balance cap: limit on the total amount that can be transferred into the retirement phase. Also the cut-off used for non-concessional cap, bring-forward, co-contribution and spouse offset eligibility.

rows.note: General cap only; an individual's personal transfer balance cap varies with their own transfer balance account history and is not modelled here.
